text: {"headline":"Elevated 99215 use is concentrated in multi-morbid patients but runs above peer rates at every complexity tier, and with only one documented 99215 claim the records are too thin to tell upcoding from a sicker panel.","leaning":"inconclusive","interpretation":"The by-complexity table shows this provider's 99215 share rising with condition count, as a complex panel would. It also sits above the all-provider share in nearly every tier, most visibly at 1, 3 and 4+ conditions, so patient mix alone does not obviously explain the excess. The billing is also heavily weighted toward 99214, which deserves attention alongside 99215. Low-complexity 99215s are a small share of the total. Sampled examples such as C0005324 (upper respiratory infection, no chronic conditions), C0006268 and C0007603 look hard to justify at the highest level on their diagnoses alone. High-complexity examples such as C0007389 and C0006068 are plausible. The single documented 99215 (C0006493) supported the billed level, and the one data-reviewed note without a lab line is weak evidence at most. With records for only 8 claims, documentation cannot settle the question. A reviewer should first request charts for the low-complexity 99215 claims and a sample of 99214 claims to check whether documented MDM and time support the billed levels."}
